links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of ChatGPT and website patient education content versus recommended 5th-6th grade
links.effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid grade level 11.9 (±1.6) for ChatGPT and 11.1 (±1.3) for website; ChatGPT more difficult to read on 4 of 5 readability scales and longer.
links.quote: Content from both the website and ChatGPT were significantly above the recommended fifth or sixth grade level for patient education, with a mean Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 11.1 (±1.3) for the website and 11.9 (±1.6) for the ChatGPT content.

links.outcome: Reading level of patient education material relative to appropriate patient reading level
links.effect: ChatGPT output mean Flesch-Kincaid grade 11.9 (±1.6) and website 11.1 (±1.3), well above the recommended fifth or sixth grade level.
links.quote: Content from both the website and ChatGPT were significantly above the recommended fifth or sixth grade level for patient education, with a mean Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 11.1 (±1.3) for the website and 11.9 (±1.6) for the ChatGPT content.

links.outcome: Factual correctness of ChatGPT answers to interventional radiology patient questions
links.effect: ChatGPT output was incorrect for 12 (11.5%) of 104 questions; PEMAT-P scores lower than website.
links.quote: The ChatGPT output was incorrect for 12 (11.5%) of 104 questions.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT's ability to generate interventional radiology patient education materials compared to a society website, assessing readability and accuracy without testing a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
